Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
"Xian" <xi...@waste.org> wrote in message
news:aj9frr$187mpi$1...@ID-123937.news.dfncis.de...

>
> > who won?
>
> As LSJ announced, Jared Strait won the NA Championship. A pretty darn tense
> game. I'll leave commentary on it to others.
>

Commentary:

I don't understand why everyone says this game is so long. I didn't have a
single game take more than an hour.

Xian's deck seemed to cause any table he even *looked* at to grind to a halt.
I can't count the number of times (okay, 2... but it seemed like more) that I
finished my game, went off for a brat, cruised the convention hall, and came
back to see him sit, stare at his cards, sigh, play with his 20-some pool, then
discard a card and say he was done. On the other hand, I have to say that he
was very honorable in his stalling. He simply refused to be sped up by the
other people at the table who were rushing to try and get an oust. I'm pretty
sure he didn't take more than 10 seconds to choose his discard. Much more
reasonable than the guy who used 5th Tradition and plunked a handful of pool
down on his vamp without counting it.

I don't think I played against any of the people who made the final. One could
say that it says something about the strength of schedule I faced, but I prefer
to think of it as wrecking any deck I came across.

And finally, I have one more word to say about the tournament... Sixth. SIXTH!
The most miserable place to hold in a V:TES tournament, especially the world
championship. I didn't even stick around to watch the final... I just went
off to wallow in a ditch.

Oh, and Xian... I'm glad that my online impressions of you were not wrong
(i.e. you were a nice guy in person as well as online). It was nice to finally
meet you, man. And the same to everyone else I met, Jeff, Josh, Fred, David
(who I don't think I've seen on this newsgroup, but to whom I offer my
apologies for siccing Julia Prima on him) everyone else who my
depression-addled mind can't remember (SIXTH!!!! SIXTH?!?!)... I'd already
met Larry and Jared, although I didn't have a chance to talk to the World
Champion-to-be this year. Tom Mickle had an absolutely amazing showing in the
qualifier (four games played, four table wins). I couldn't figure out exactly
what his deck did, but he obviously played it very well.

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
"Peter D Bakija" <PD...@bigplanet.com> wrote in message
news:B97D3904.6C79%PD...@bigplanet.com...

> So for those of us who couldn't make it (I, sadly, was on a beach with my
> wife, eating lobster...), who won? What are some good tales of action and
> adventure? Cummon--you can't *all* be sleeping it off still...

Don't be so sure. It was a long long week. The days and events all blurred
together so I may be confusing a bunch of this stuff.

SUNDAY August 4:

A bit of Chaos as flights in the Chicago area were being delayed or cancelled
due ot bad weather. Alex Harmon rented a car and drove the last leg from
Chicago. Ben Peal arrived very very late, etc. By evening we had 15 of the 16
Week of Nightmares participants plus Errol Treppanier. I think Fred Scott
arrived Saturday too but it's really hard to remember. We drank till about 3
AM. It was very hot and humid and that mixed badly with my cigar and Mike
Courtois' cigarette. We continued our games without pausing for the visit by
the fire department as they tried to determine the cause of the ceaseless shriek
of the smoke alarm.

MONDAY August 5:

Up at around 9:00 AM, we wandered into Perkins Restaurant and ate. Then we
talked to the hotel management. They said we had to be quiet at night. We got
put on a schedule and were asked to keep it down late at night. They also gave
us two round tables for our 3rd floor suite in case we ran out of room in the
bar. Some drunk chicks walked in *our* bar making all kinds of noise. She said
"What are you guysssss playinnnnn?" After she found out about the vampires, she
made a quick exit. She was desperate for male companionship...but not *that*
desperate. We had maybe 20 people there by then? I suppose we drank and played
till maybe 3:00 or 4:00 AM.

TUESDAY August 6:

Drinking and playing again. All day. All night. IIRC, this is when Matt
Heslin arrived with some friends (including Amy and a guy who she teased
mercilessly about being Jewish). We also had another *incident*. Seems one of
the folks in the bar had a little too much to drink and decided to go swimming.
The hotel's night manager said that if he went back in she'd have to call the
cops. It seems the hotel chain's president was staying in the hotel that
evening. Of course, I said I'd make sure our friend didn't go back in. Well,
hell, I was in the middle of a game for cryin' out loud. Cut me some slack!
Next thing I know he disappeared and I rushed to the glass door to the pool
area. Fortunately there were no V:TES players floating face-down. Mike
Courtois and I decided to go look around. We found our friend crashed out in
front of the door to his suite. We read him a bedtime story and tucked him in.

WEDNESDAY:
Hardcore play and drink day. We registerd at GenCon Wednesday evening. I think
we played a couple of Rapid Thought tournaments this evening. Sleep around 3 or
4 AM and up early for half of us.

THURSDAY:
Rapid Thought at the con. Most people drank and played till around 4:00 AM. This
may have also been the night we played poker. Some fools played-out some games
till dawn. I believe we had all of the tables in the bar full at this point and
there were 41 V:TES players here by this evening.

FRIDAY:

After getting up at 9:00 AM to drive some people to the con, I returned to the
hotel to take a day off with a number of people. Got some much needed rest as
it was the first day with more than maybe 4 or 5 hours of sleep. We repeated
the madness friday night playing and drinking. Each day was like the other.

SATURDAY:

Final Qualifier: I sat as Paul Johnson's predator in the final and bled like a
maniac. He cycled into another deflection and sent my unblockable bleeds down
the line. Paul and Tom Mickle went to the time limit. Then we went and drank
more and played more. With the wake-up calls set for 6:30 AM, we knew we had to
get to bed early. Few were smart enough to do what needed to be done and we
stayed up really late anyway.

SUNDAY:

N.A. Championships:
Round 1: I sat as Jared's predator, with my predator being Noal McDonald and
grand predator Ben Swainbank. My grand prey was Matt Hirsch. Ben and Jared
went to the finals later so this was an early preview. Jared showed a Nos
prince with potence so I waited until I had Roxanne: Rectrix 13th and Ozmo ready
to bring up simultaneously. I lived a while and dug into Jared for some huge
bleeds. I crippled him good. I also incurred the wrath of the table. Jared
and Ben Swainbank swapped table positions. Ben incurred the same heavy bleeds
and I came up one card short of ousting him. There was a lot of good table
talk. Noal was killing me and no one cared...much. Jared looked like he was
about to end his turn and I suggested he send Noal's famous vamp to torpor to
oust him. I was pleased to hear Noal call me a "fucker". Didn't matter in the
end. Jared ousted Noal with a vote. I had one vamp sent to torpor and the
other was Pentex'd and empty. With only a few pool left I still couldn't get
anyone at the table to release me from my cage. I figured if they wouldn't help
me I'm certainly not going to do them the favor of dying slowly for them. I
transfered myself out that turn. Jared now had 2 vps. Ben Swainback eventually
ousted Jared for table win.

ROUND 2: I got a table win and a sweep. Long story here but basically I had
Darby Keeney playing a great 1st Trad deck. He tried to help the table to keep
me from ousting my prey but Darby's assistance was squandered turn after turn as
they kept bleeding each other. I initally tried to bleed responsibly but after
they were all working together I decided to just let loose. Darby's predator
spend himself down to 1 pool to bring up Moncada. Go figure. He deflected so
much early that I figured he had 20 of them. I bled him out eventually as it
turned out that he, somehow had no deflections. With my last minion I bled
Darby so hard he couldn't pay for his own three first traditions.

Also in this round, Alex Harmon died from a Contingency Planning played when he
had 1 pool left. Very little combat and I never saw a grapple the whole day.

FINALS:

Szilan was building a Cardano deck that used Ankara Citadel to play free Freak
Drives, free Deflections, free 5th trad, free Skin of Steel etc. Trey Morita
smacked his predator into oblivion with War Ghoul attacks. Jared's pool
situation was much better than the other players and he was calling votes
uncontested. Trey's intercept was no match for the forgotten labyrinth. His
death was imminent. Rather than working together to squash Jared, Ben and Trey
seemed pretty content to just try to kill their own prey before Jared got to
them. In the end, it seemed to just line the table up for Jared. Jared got
Trey and Ben in one vote, giving Jared a 2nd Vp, Trey 1 VP, and ensuring himself
at least a tie. With Jared assured of the tournament win, he then conceded the
rest of the game to Szilan to make sure he had plenty of time to catch his
flight. Very little table-talk in contrast to last year's event.

-Robert

OK, I'm pretty sure that this deck cost me my spot in the finals, since
that round went to time, and I think Alex Hammon agreed that I would've
gotten him with a Samedji'd Natalia, two pool/turn bloat, and a Fortune
Teller Shop in play, aside from whatever else I might've played. However,
it was probably the best game I participated in, and Xian's deck certainly
had the tools to oust. From what I could tell of it, it certainly wasn't
an "I block everything and bloat" deck. Still, I believe *every* round
that he played went to time, and that's saying something.

I can understand that time limits are a necessary evil, but I don't like them
very much, and I think I'd like to see the limit raised to two and a half
hours, since many games that time out seem to be on the verge of
concluding. I realize, however, that this isn't likely to happen given
the amount of time one tournament already consumes. I'd guess that this
has been thought over by the powers that be, and the (apparent) effort
being made to speed up games is the alternative solution.

> Oh, and Xian... I'm glad that my online impressions of you were not wrong

Seconded, one hundred and ten percent. I met, and dug, many, many players
that I knew only from the newsgroup, and Xian was among the coolest.

David Cherryholmes
Prince of Durham, NC

Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 13 Aug 2002, Peter D Bakija wrote:

> This gets brought up a lot, but that is the same for any deck. If any deck
> works in VTES, it works by denying its opponent the ability to play the
> game.

It getting "brought up a lot" wouldn't, maybe, make you think there might
be something to it, would it?

> Sure, if I Rush and burn my prey's 6 point vampire, he is out of a vampire,
> and thus I limit his ability to do anything (i.e. play). How is that really
> any different than if I simply bleed my prey for 6? That 6 pool could have
> been a vampire that could do things. As I bled my prey for 6 pool, he is
> effectively out a 6 pool vampire.

It's the difference between "could have been" and "is." In the latter
case, he has a minion in the game and six less pool; he plays the
game. In the former case, he has no minion and six extra pool; he stares
at his hand. This whole analysis is a little over-simplified by talking
in terms of one minion. Usually there are several, and dunking one will
have an effect on the controlling player's game, but does not shut it down
completely. And since most decks will speak to combat in some form or
fashion, the only deck that will reliably eliminate *all* the minions you
want is... what? Class? That's right: the weenie deck!

> Sure, when a Rush deck works, its prey doesn't get to do much ('cause his
> vampires are all dead). But when a S+B deck works, its prey doesn't get to
> do much either ('cause he is ousted). The only real difference is that with
> the S+B deck, you get to get up and leave the table a few minutes earlier.

Feh. In the stealth bleed case, he has minions that can deflect, or rush
backwards, or whatever, and then he maybe dies. In the case of weenie
rush, he brings up minions, they go to torpor, repeat ad nauseum until dead.
Or, he refuses to bring up minions, gets bled for one a lot while he stares at
the game he would've played, then dies.

The really comparable case would be weenie presence vote, weenie presence
bleed, or weenie dominate bleed, usually aggravated by anarch revolts which
either speed up the process or drag everyone else's game down by causing
them to burn a bunch of minion actions to get rid of the damn things. With
those three decks as your predator, you will probably lose so much pool so
fast that your game will never get going. Maybe the next prey down the
line will be OK with the time you bought him, but you are fucked.

Weenie presence, weenie potence, weenie dominate. What say we tip a glass
to these dangerous machines, and to their inventors and the craftsmen
who've honed them over the years. Then, let's lock them away and end the
detente. I think our game will be a lot better for it. YMMV.



Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 13 Aug 2002, Peter D Bakija wrote:

> Of course! Just like card limits!

Oh. Those people. Well, they're wrong and I'm right. That's the
distinction. ;) And actually, the only "card limit argument" I've seen in
years has been "man, I know my group sucks but I'm stuck with card limits
so here's my deck."

> > It's the difference between "could have been" and "is." In the latter
> > case, he has a minion in the game and six less pool; he plays the
> > game.

> Not if losing that 6 pool ousts him. Again, if I am a Rush deck, and I kill
> 16 pool worth of vampires, my prey is out 16 pool and 16 pool worth of
> vampires. If I am a S+B deck, and I bleed my prey for 16, that is 16 less
> pool they have to spend on vampires, and as a result, they are out 16 pool
> and 16 pool worth of vampires. In either case, they are likely to be dead
> soon anyways, so it doesn't really matter.

Notice the switch from six to sixteen. It's a significant shift of the
premise. If you've bled him for sixteen, then you've gotten up three
mid-caps, or you're swarming with weenie dominate. I agree with you
Peter, weenie potence rush is not one jot worse (or better) than weenie
dominate. If it's the midcaps, that took time, and he's playing the
game. That's what this is all about, to me: decks that don't let the
other guy play the game.

> > Feh. In the stealth bleed case, he has minions that can deflect, or rush
> > backwards, or whatever, and then he maybe dies.
>
> Or he doesn't have any minions, 'cause he was bled a lot and couldn't afford
> to bring them out.

You snipped the part of my post where I addressed this ahead of
time. Will a Malk deck bleed out it's prey before it can get a minion
out? In the odd case of a burgeoning, behemoth, "here's my guy" deck that
didn't see any of its influence-enhancers.... possibly. In any other
case, that guy's going to get up a minion or two, and pitch his deck's
answer to stealth-bleed at his predators three or four minions. It's the
weenie decks that do what you're talking about, and I'm not drawing any
distinctions between your deck and any other loop-holing power weenie
deck.



Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
David Cherryholmes wrote:

> By "Rush Deck" you mean "Weenie Rush Deck" right? Otherwise, you drop the
> "easily" and replace it with something like "doable." I dunno, maybe I'm
> bogging down on the semantics. I suppose the only really reliable rush
> decks *are* going to need an overwhelming number of rush actions for that
> tactic to float a table win on it's own.

Sure--I think by deffenition, any Rush deck that is going to be half way
viable is going to have an average vampire size of, like, +/- 3.5. I think
any Rush deck that has substantially larger vampires (like an average size
of 6+) is more of a larky, "fun" deck, rather than a viable tournament
comtender.

> In any case, my premise has never been that this isn't an effective tactic,
> just that it's fuck-all no fun for anyone else playing against it.

Which is a reasonable statement (although not completely correct--at
Origins, when I was not playing my Rush deck, and I was sitting between 2
Rush decks, I had a very fun game, but that is me), but again, can apply to
any really effective deck. A really fast bleed deck? No fun to be the prey
of. An Anarch Revolt deck? No fun to be the prey of. A steamroller vote
deck? No fun to be the prey of. A "Intercept everything and Obediance" deck?
No fun to be the predator of. Any fast, effective deck isn't going to be fun
tobe next to, if by "fun" you mean "getting to play for a long time and
getting your deck to do what it is supposed to do". That is part of
competetive play.



> That's what this is all about, to me: decks that don't let the

I agree with this completely, and agree that it is unfortunate. Sadly,
however, it is the state of the game. Most decks that do really well do so
by denying its opposition from doing much.

Yes, it would be great if this were not the case. It would take a
significant change to the game structure to make it happen, however, like
eliminating all vampires in the game with a capacity less than 4 or
something. If there are weenie vampres (cap 1-3), regardless of their
disciplines, there will be weenie speed decks that are incredibly effective
when compared to most decks built around cap 5+ vampires.
